description: DR POWER, the Data Repository for Power system Open models With Evolving Resources, is an open repository of power grid models and scenarios at egriddata.org, funded by ARPA-E's GRID DATA programme and run jointly by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and the National Rural Electric Cooperative Association. The pages read on 2026-09-26 say it holds over 272,700 curated datasets with more than a million downloadable files, has had users in 142 countries since its launch in July 2017, and runs version 3.0. Publishing groups include the Electric Grid Test Case Repository of synthetic grids hosted by Texas A&M University, the Grid Optimization Competition datasets, MATPOWER test cases, the UW Power Systems Test Case Archive, the Pacific Northwest Smart Grid Demonstration, University of Wisconsin-Madison GRID DATA sets and NREL solar and wind data. Coverage is transmission, distribution, generation, market and weather data contributed by laboratories, universities and projects, much of it from the United States, plus synthetic networks. Anyone can browse and download files at no cost; registered users can upload data, have it curated and request DOIs. Formats and licences vary by dataset. Caveats: the site itself flags the NREL solar and wind copies as poor quality, and curation depth differs between groups. Simulation uses are testing optimal power flow and grid optimisation algorithms, network flow studies and resilience analysis on realistic but non-confidential grids. Related records: data-tamu-electric-grid-test-cases is the synthetic grid collection, and data-arpa-e-grid-optimization-competition holds the competition datasets.
